annotations.title: Say what a transaction’s cash turned into

description: Name the holding a transaction bought or sold, and how much of it — **a list in one call**. Such a row is cash turning into a holding inside one account (a broker buying a fund, a savings account opening a deposit): it counts in neither came in, went out nor moved, and the holding’s quantity is the sum of its rows’ quantities. `quantity` is a count of the thing, never money — bought is positive, sold negative, up to six places. `holding: null` clears both. The holding must sit at a place that names the row’s own account, or at one that names none, and is never an account’s own cash. Holdings and their ids are listed by `savings`; transaction ids by `transactions`. **Dry-runs by default**; the document is copied to a timestamped .bak first.

commit.description: Default false. False previews; true writes.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

rows.description: One entry per transaction. Up to 500 in a call.

holding.description: The holding, by id or by a name only one holding carries; null clears it.

quantity.description: How much of the holding: positive bought, negative sold. Required with a holding.
